themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization has no stable rank or impression log, cross-channel incrementality faces platforms that change delivery mid-test, identity resolution has no verified list of who is really the same person, B2B buying-group intent has almost no confirmed outcomes, content governance has reviewers who disagree with each other, and today's ad supply integrity answers say verifying an impression costs real money while faking one costs almost nothing.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blocker is often money and politics, inside the company as well as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models would build a fast lane with perks so declaring beats spoofing, on journey orchestration they note channel bonuses reward sending more, on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions a political settlement, and on ad supply integrity they say participants resist transparency and the side with the budget is not clearly motivated to find the answer.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: All three models answer safe agent execution with a proxy or gateway holding the credentials and enforcing spend, rate and audience caps, consent enforcement with a single checkpoint on every path data leaves, and journey orchestration with one shared contact log every channel must check before sending.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from the outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removal from an already-trained model, on incrementality they say platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and on answer engines they say retrieval and weights expose no ranking logs.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what counts as a good outcome, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three would lock generation to a registry of approved claims because deciding whether wording is still supported is contextual judgment, on the semantic context layer they argue two teams can both be right about what revenue means, and on journey orchestration they say no single metric compares a conversion against customer harm.
